title: Proxy Reception
text: “Hey, Time Drive—where’s Shadow Saint?”
Kuro-chan tugged at the hem of my clothes, asking. Indeed, Ren was nowhere to be seen. What I did see was the adventurer who’d become Ren’s subordinate.
“Is Ren not coming, I wonder?”
“Ren-sama entrusted this round’s reward collection to me.”
“What! Is he really that averse to seeing Kuro-chan, I say!”

There’s only so much rudeness one can excuse. Ren, the only reason I’ve been letting you slide is because you’re Kuro-chan’s playmate. After playing together so much yesterday, has the thought of playing happily together again really not crossed your mind?
“No… he said he was rather displeased by what happened yesterday. When I asked if it was because that child was too intense, he said that wasn’t it.”
Oh? Ren’s subordinate was offering some mysterious cover for him, indeed.
“This is just my personal impression, but although she can be strict, I saw in that child’s kindness toward someone so young the true qualities of a hero.”
“Boo…”
“That said, my honest feeling is I’d rather she not get too tangled up with Ren-sama. He’s still not fully recovered, after all.”

Are you seriously suggesting that even a full day later, Kuro-chan’s elegant tipsiness still hasn’t worn off? She’s not that fragile, I say. Faking illness won’t do, Ren. Still, there are various things I’ll need to keep an eye on.
“Well then, Kuro-chan, go find Ren later and play with him, indeed.”
“Okaaay—Kuro will go invite Shadow Saint into the darkness—”
“You really ought to go, dear. If Kuro keeps playing around, that strange way of speaking might rub off on the other children, and that would be troublesome, dear.”

Yuki-chan seemed to approve of Kuro-chan going out. Apparently, because Kuro-chan was the very first Filolial-sama I raised in this loop, some of the others occasionally recognized her as a sort of leader. Kuro-chan, if anything, was the type of Filolial-sama who preferred playing with one specific person rather than running with the pack. Not exactly leader material, I say.
“I would really rather she didn’t come, if possible…”
“Ren will get used to it eventually, I say. He’ll be having fun playing before he knows it.”
If Kuro-chan is the one to wake him, Ren can rest easy too.
“Yay!”

Now then… the Filo-tan Plan has been set into motion, but I still need to think about what comes after, up through the next Wave. It’s not just the Wave in Melromarc—I’ll need to make various trips to Waves occurring elsewhere too. If I don’t suppress the Waves at least somewhat, there’s a strong chance Rival will seize the opportunity to cross over into this world. Ideally, I need to seal the worlds apart permanently so that Rival can never come here again.

Which reminds me—in the loop where I was reunited with Fleon-chan, even after the Wave ended, Rival still made it back to this world. It seems the other world has some kind of ship capable of crossing over to this one. Is there no way to destroy that thing, I wonder? Just as I was pondering this, a memory surfaced in my mind of Raph-chan—the Raph-species made from Big Sister’s own hair—riding aboard that very ship. …That thing might just be indestructible, I say. Either way, things are only going to keep getting busier from here.
Trash came shuffling over. Seeing Éclair, he saluted as if minding his place in line and stood waiting, indeed.
“…Now then, let us proceed with distributing the reward money and relief funds for this Wave.”

Naturally, Trash and the Crimson Swine had apparently thrown a fit last night. Things hadn’t gone the way they wanted, and tantrums had ensued. As for the Crimson Swine, being called ugly and looked down upon with contempt by Father seemed to have put it in a particularly foul mood—I could hear the soldiers grumbling about it. Well, apparently the Queen’s faction’s shadow pig had reported things in such a way that issuing a wanted notice for Éclair’s “prison escape” was no longer possible. I caught wind of that exchange too.
“Now then, to each of the heroes.”

Bags full of silver coins were brought forward. Two bags, was it? Naturally, there was none for Father—he’d said he didn’t want any, after all. One must be for Itsuki, and the rest for Ren? Where is mine, I wonder? Oi, Trash, what is the meaning of this, I say! I readied Brionac as a means of intimidation.
“Ahem!”
The moment Trash cleared his throat, another bag was brought forward. Yes, yes, that’s more like it, I say.

“First, Itsuki-dono… your accomplishments echo throughout the kingdom. You have completed that difficult task admirably and fought for the sake of the nation. Including an apology and medical compensation for last night’s incident, this comes to nine thousand five hundred silver coins.”

Quite the increase, I see. Ninety-five gold coins’ worth. Heh… go ahead and bask in your sense of superiority over such petty change, I say. Itsuki jingled the coins as he checked the contents of the bag, glancing my way. Then he looked toward the bag apparently meant for me, and back at me again.
“Considering you barely did anything and just watched, being Naofumi’s little tagalong, that amount sounds about right.”
Same old story—running his mouth about things that make my blood boil like it’s his job. You’re nothing but Fleon-chan’s plaything, you hear me! Take this, you New Nambu!
“Next, Ren-dono… or rather, his proxy. Adding the reward for accomplishments against the Wave along with the completed request, that comes to two thousand three hundred silver coins.”
Oh? That’s quite a reduction in reward, I noticed.

“What?! Ren-sama contributed the most against the Wave! Why is there such a disparity?! Ren-sama already harbors distrust toward Melromarc from everything that’s happened. For the sake of our future relations, I ask that you reconsider, once again.”

The representative of Ren’s subordinates protested, indeed. Well, he had a point. Now that I thought about it, these people had originally been adventurers arranged by Melromarc. By this point, it seemed their loyalty to Ren had come to outweigh that. Given the disgraceful display last night, that was hardly surprising.

“I see. Ren-san… working together with the person standing over there, dealt more damage to the boss than I did. And yet, given this reward, one has to wonder if there wasn’t some private arrangement involved.”
Itsuki voiced his agreement with Trash’s allocation.
“Ngh…”
“Surely this isn’t a case where, despite launching an attack like that, his reward was docked simply because he didn’t agree with something?”
Itsuki’s hostility had grown considerably. He looked thoroughly obnoxious, practically spoiling for a fight with everyone around him. I suppose that just goes to show how well Father had performed.
“It appears there was a discrepancy in the reports. Factoring in his contribution to the Wave, I shall add a further fifteen hundred silver coins.”

Additional silver was brought over and stuffed into the bag. Honestly, if they insist on paying in silver, I do wish they’d consider the sheer quantity involved. Both Itsuki and Ren’s subordinates looked burdened, clutching their bags with expressions that said the jingling excess was more trouble than it was worth. There’s such a thing as prioritizing appearances too much, I say.

Oi… Trash, hand over my reward money properly, I say. Kuro-chan fought valiantly alongside Ren, after all. Which means I demand you add Kuro-chan’s share of the achievement on top of my base reward. And so, I leveled an intimidating demand at Trash to cough up the coin.

“Kuro-chan ran across the battlefield right alongside Ren, I say—the Wave boss was practically finished off by Kuro-chan, wasn’t it—? Ah, and Father’s slave was quite the star too, taking off its head, wasn’t she—? Don’t tell me you’ve forgotten, I say—?”
“Grrgh…”
“You should really be more humble. Bragging about yourself like that is unsightly. It’s exactly that attitude that makes the King torment you and Naofumi-san.”
Quiet, Itsuki, I say. You’re one to talk, getting pummeled by spells raining down under Trash’s own orders—what exactly are you spouting off about?
“Hmph, I’m simply stating facts. Above all, isn’t it a fact that Naofumi-san attacked Princess Malty?”
Are you still buying into that nonsense, I wonder? If you don’t wake up soon, even my patience is nearing its limit, I say.
I’ve decided. Before I awaken Itsuki with Fleon-chan, I’m going to show him a taste of hell.
